prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1366; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the insured's representing attorney's office following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The insured vehicle was struck from behind while stopped, and the claimant reports neck pain and whiplash symptoms.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver of the insured vehicle is named on the policy and that coverage was active at the time of loss. Policy records show no lapse or recent changes that would affect this claim.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and notes the rear impact. Responding officers recorded the vehicle positions but no independent witnesses were identified.

Entry 4: Received scene and vehicle photographs from the claimant. They confirm the general location of the impact and the rear damage, though they do not show every detail the claimant describes.

Entry 5: Reviewed the vehicle appraisal. Damage appears consistent with a rear impact of this type, but it is not yet clear whether all of the listed damage resulted from this collision. A supplemental inspection has been requested.

Entry 6: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who provided the medical file. The reported whiplash injury is a kind that fits the force and direction of this impact, and no earlier injury to the same body area is known from the records provided.

Entry 7: Recorded the claimant's statement through counsel. It added some minor details not mentioned at first notice, but the core account of the collision has stayed the same across each telling.

Entry 8: Reviewed the treatment records. Care followed a usual course of physical therapy and medication, and the claimant's symptoms eased steadily as treatment progressed.

Entry 9: Checked prior claims and vehicle history for the insured vehicle. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on record, and nothing suggests any of the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 10: Requested the claimant's remaining treatment and billing records through counsel. Updated the reserve to reflect the current treatment status and the pending supplemental vehicle inspection.

Entry 11: Discussed status with the claimant's attorney. Treatment has tapered as the claimant improved, and the file will remain open pending receipt of the final billing records and the supplemental inspection report.
